## Changes with compatibility implications

- Metabuild is updated to Scala 3.9.
- Apache Ivy is removed from the dependency.

### Scala 3.9

sbt 2.1.0 updates the Scala version used by the metabuild to Scala 3.9.0 LTS.

Since both sbt 2.x and Scala 3.x are only backward compatible across minor versions, appropriate Scala version must be used for building sbt plugins:

| sbt 2.x | Scala 3.x | Plugin works on sbt 2.0.x | Works on sbt 2.1.x |
| ------: | --------: | :-----------------------: | :------------------: |
|   2.0.x |     3.8.x |            ✅             |            ✅        |
|   2.1.0 |     3.9.x |            ❌             |            ✅        |

While publishing plugins using sbt 2.1.0 would mean that it would no longer be compatible with sbt 2.0.x, given that Scala 3.9 is an LTS that will be supported for the next 3 years, we should use it as a new baseline. Here's how to set the minimal sbt version for your plugin:

```scala
pluginCrossBuild / sbtVersion := {
  scalaBinaryVersion.value match {
    case "2.12" => "1.9.9"
    case _      => "2.1.0"
  }
}
```

### Publishing

sbt 2.1.0 removes Apache Ivy from its transitive dependency, and implements Ivyless publishing.

This was contributed by @bitloi, @fury0928, @BrianHotopp, @mkurz, @stasimus, @jozanek, and @eed3si9n in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8686, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8866, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8894, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8975, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8988, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8996, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9069, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9463, and https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9533, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9615, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9756, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9804, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9806, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9811, https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9814 etc.

## Test summary

When tests are executed, sbt 2.1.0 displays a test summary at the end, listing the failed test suites as follows:

```bash
[error] Test summary (2 test tasks failed):
[error]   a / Test / testQuick
[error]         com.example.a.TestA     FAIL
[error]   b / Test / testQuick
[error]         com.example.b.TestB     FAIL
[error]
[error] failed: total 4, failed 2, errors 0, passed 2, cached 2
```

Successful tests will display only a terse summary by default:

```bash
[info] passed: total 4, failed 0, errors 0, passed 4, cached 4
```

`--test_summary=success` can override the behavior to list the successful test as well. Test summary was contributed by @eed3si9n and @BrianHotopp in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9602 + https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9214.

## Test cache opt-out

sbt 2.1.0 can let you opt out of test result caching:

```bash
$ sbt test --cache_test_result=false
```

This was contributed by @anatoliykmetyuk in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9675.

## workerMaxInstances and testTopology 

sbt 2.1.0 adds new settings `workerMaxInstances` and `testTopology` to control test scheduling,
especially of the forked tests. Use `Global / workerMaxInstances` to change the number of worker instances. The default is set to 2:

```scala
// or sbt -Dsbt.worker_max_instances=2
Global / workerMaxInstances := 2
```

Use the `testTopology` setting to control whether you want to split the test classes into multiple workers or keep them together. The default was changed to split to 2 groups:

```scala
Test / testTopology := TestTopology.subprojectSplit(2)
```

To keep all classes in a subproject on one worker instead, use:

```scala
Test / testTopology := TestTopology.subprojectExclusive
```

This was contributed by @eed3si9n in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9665

## clean task

sbt 2.1.0 updates the `clean` task to act as a cache invalidator. Regardless of the cache state, running `clean` would invalidate the cache for the next command execution. This can be scoped to subproject or configuration:

```bash
$ sbt foo/clean
$ sbt foo/compile
```

This was contributed by @eed3si9n in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9752

## Source dependency update

sbt 2.1.0 provides better control to handle source dependencies.

This was contributed by @seroperson in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/8880.

## Identity map optimization

In sbt 2.1.0, a key assignment (`:=`) whose right-hand side is `expr.value` short-circuits to `x.set(expr)`.
This is helpful in avoiding `JsonFormat[A]` when `expr` is an uncached task.

This was contributed by @eed3si9n in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9831

## Task-level caching opt-out

```scala
// opt out of compilation cache
Compile / compile / cacheStores := Nil
Test / compile / cacheStores := Nil

// opt out of test cache
Test / test / cacheStores := Nil
```

This was contributed by @eed3si9n in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9874

### Input-only cache

sbt 2.1.0 introduces a new cache level `CacheLevelTag.InputOnly`:

```scala
@cacheLevel(include = Array(CacheLevelTag.InputOnly))
val scalacOptions = taskKey[Seq[String]]("Options for the Scala compiler.")
```

Similar to `Def.uncached(...)`, `scalacOptions` will evaluate each time, but `scalacOptions.value` will participate as an input to other cached task.

This was contributed by @eed3si9n in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9953

## HTTP Bazel cache

sbt 2.1.0 adds support for HTTP Bazel cache, in addition to gPRC.

```scala
Global / remoteCache := Some(uri("http://127.0.0.1:8000"))
```

This was contributed by @eed3si9n in https://github.com/sbt/sbt/pull/9880
